ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, and $AC=6$. The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point C to obtain $\triangle A'B'C'$, where point A' happens to be on side AB. What is the distance between point B' and point B?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $B'B$.\\
$\because$ Triangle $ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain $\triangle A'B'C$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=A'C$, $AB=A'B$, $\angle A=\angle CA'B'=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AA'C$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AA'C=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B'A'B=180^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ Triangle $ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain $\triangle A'B'C$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACA'=\angle BAB'=60^\circ$, $BC=B'C$, $\angle CB'A'=\angle CBA=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BCB'$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CB'B=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CB'A'=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A'B'B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B'BA'=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, $AC=6$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=12$,\\
$\therefore$ $A'B=AB−AA'=AB−AC=6$,\\
$\therefore$ $B'B=6\sqrt{3}$,\\
Therefore, the answer is: \boxed{6\sqrt{3}}.

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, and $AC=6$. The triangle $\triangle ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain $\triangle A'B'C'$, where point $A'$ happens to be on side $AB$. What is the distance between point $B'$ and point $B$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line $B'B$.\\
$\because$ Triangle $ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain $\triangle A'B'C$,\\
$\therefore$ $AC=A'C$, $AB=A'B$, $\angle A=\angle CA'B'=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AA'C$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AA'C=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B'A'B=180^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ Triangle $ABC$ is rotated counterclockwise around point $C$ to obtain $\triangle A'B'C$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACA'=\angle BAB'=60^\circ$, $BC=B'C$, $\angle CB'A'=\angle CBA=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BCB'$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CB'B=60^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle CB'A'=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A'B'B=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B'BA'=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ=90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $\angle A=60^\circ$, $AC=6$,\\
$\therefore$ $AB=12$,\\
$\therefore$ $A'B=AB-AA'=AB-AC=6$,\\
$\therefore$ $B'B=6\sqrt{3}$,\\
Therefore, the answer is $\boxed{6\sqrt{3}}$.
